clue.text: Small bow when Monsieur makes scornful remarks

parts.note: an arc is a bow shape, as in a rainbow's arc
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun set'
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, French for Mr

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's curt bow is taken as a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting mockery, so it is a name for scornful remarks collectively.

clue.text: Lay off only producer of old music

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss or lay off from work
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A redundant worker is the only one making old-fashioned music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay off' reads as a command to stop, but it is the verb for dismissing staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early trombone, so an instrument that produced Renaissance music.

clue.text: Scan fitting to make new modifications

parts.note: to scan text is to read it
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A scan shows a fitting needs new adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to adjust again, which is making fresh modifications.

clue.text: In Arabic, the injunction for a martyr

parts.note: al is the Arabic definite article
a ban is a prohibition or injunction

explanation.surface: An Arabic decree concerns a martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: St Alban is honoured as Britain's first Christian martyr.

clue.text: Cocktail spread? For the last two, cheers!

indicators.note: the last two letters of the spread are swapped for the word for thanks

parts.note: margarine is a spread for bread
ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A drinks party spread is laid on, and a final toast goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the last two' swaps NE at the end of MARGARINE for TA. 'Cheers' here is a British thank-you, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila and lime cocktail.

clue.text: Note development of a cult based on truth

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a development reshapes something, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cult that grows up around a musical note claims to rest on fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' shuffles both A and CULT; the note is FA from sol-fa, not a letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something factual is grounded in real events, which is what being based on truth means.

clue.text: What makes a head is a face, ignoring new head of hair

indicators.note: the new-letter is left out of the face word

parts.note: a front is a face, as of a building

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A face without a new hairstyle is what gives someone a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes N from FRONT, giving FROT, then H. The head here is the foam on a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is the foam that forms the head on a glass of beer.

clue.text: Something to keep a lid on bonds, barring a pitfall

definitions.text: Something to keep a lid on

indicators.note: barring means except, so the letter is left out

parts.note: chains are bonds or fetters
a trap is a pitfall

explanation.surface: Restraints keep a lid on things, except where a trap lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barring' removes A from CHAINS to give CHINS. The lid is a hat or helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinstrap holds a helmet or hat on the head, and lid is slang for a hat or helmet.

clue.text: Snubbing knight, do the opposite of commending place in high position

indicators.note: to snub is to ignore, so the knight letter is left out

parts.note: to unpraise is to withhold praise or disparage
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a knight and, far from praising, elevates another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbing' drops N from UNPRAISE, a rare word for withholding praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to raise up or exalt, so to lift into a high position.

clue.text: Mild disagreement from Becker over stopping obstructed serve

indicators.note: the turned letters plug the middle of the serve word

parts.note: a let in tennis is a serve that clips the net and is replayed

indicators.note: these letters are turned over, read backwards in the down entry

parts.note: Boris Becker, the German tennis player, would say nein, German for no

explanation.surface: Becker mildly disputes a serve that hit the net.
explanation.walkthrough: Becker is the German tennis star, so his 'no' is in German; 'over' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means gentle or forgiving, so mild in its judgment.

clue.text: Room cleaner receiving honour

indicators.note: the cleaner takes in the honour, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner is presented with an award.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British cleaning woman; the MBE is a British honour given in the New Year and Birthday lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a formal word for a room, as in a council chamber.

clue.text: A travesty of moronic character

indicators.note: a travesty is a grotesque distortion, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's character is mocked as idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a description of a person, but it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Shower with plugs to knock pressure on the head?

indicators.note: the shower and the with-letter fill a gap in the knocking word, as a plug fills a hole

parts.note: to bash is to knock or strike hard
a shower of rain

explanation.surface: Someone takes a shower and then knocks their head on the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic, signalled by the question mark: forced indoctrination is pressure applied to the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainwashing is coercive persuasion of the mind, playfully described as pressure applied to the head.

clue.text: Winter sportsperson mostly restricting velocity, to take it easy

indicators.note: the shortened word hems in the next letter, which sits inside it
most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a skier does a winter sport
v is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A skier slows down to have an easy time on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of SKIER, giving SKIE, and V goes inside. To skive is British slang for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: To skive is to shirk duties and idle, a colloquial way to take it easy.

clue.text: Unique object identifier after computing back tax

indicators.note: the identifier comes after the turned-round letters
the computing letters are turned round

parts.note: IT, information technology, is computing
the definite article the picks out one unique object

explanation.surface: A computing ID tag, then back taxes are owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI. 'the' is called a unique object identifier because the definite article marks one particular thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid as a levy to the church, so it is a tax.

clue.text: English heather overruns lush, little-known stuff

indicators.note: the heather runs on past the drunkard, coming after it

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, as is a sot
Erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: English heather grows wild over a lush, obscure patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' looks like an adjective for the heather but is a noun for a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure matters known only to a few, so little-known stuff.

clue.text: In this month, recommend name connected with revolt

indicators.note: In tells us to put the next pieces inside the month abbreviation

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old business letters
to urge is to recommend strongly

explanation.surface: A letter this month advises naming someone tied to an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is an old commercial-letter abbreviation for 'this month', and 'In' places URGE and N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel, so the adjective describes anything tied to a rebellion.

clue.text: Resent fussing about small motivating payment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece
fussing about stirs things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of resent are used as written
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A cross person resents fussing over a small incentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resent' looks like the verb of the surface but is the anagram fodder; 'about' wraps it round the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe offered to persuade someone.

clue.text: Identify men about to block certain replacement

indicators.note: the turned letters obstruct the middle of the next word, sitting inside it

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: these letters are turned round

parts.note: to tag something is to label or identify it
OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Men are told to identify themselves to stop a sure stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round both the identifying word and the men together before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute standing in for someone else, so a replacement.

clue.text: Callow youth forming attachments with no end of excitement

indicators.note: the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: stapling fastens papers together

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An inexperienced youngster forms relationships without much excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of excitement' removes T from STAPLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, and figuratively a raw, inexperienced young person.

clue.text: Republican doctors denied initial source of stories

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it

explanation.surface: A Republican's doctors are refused the first source of stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' is a verb here: to doctor a pet is to neuter it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is an international news agency, supplying news stories to papers.

clue.text: Penny and Oscar have a meeting put forward

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a committee sits when it meets

explanation.surface: Two people named Penny and Oscar meet and propose something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny and Oscar' look like two people but give P and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to propose an idea for consideration, so to put it forward.

clue.text: Edge of Swiss roll around — what to do with it?

indicators.note: the outermost, first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to wallow is to roll around, as in mud

explanation.surface: A slice from the edge of a Swiss roll: what to do with it?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back through the whole clue: what you do with a Swiss roll is eat it. 'roll around' is not part of the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowing is what you do with cake once bitten, so the action is the answer to the question.

clue.text: Unknown people accepting charge for counselling?

indicators.note: the people word takes the charge inside it

parts.note: they means unspecified people, as in 'they say'
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: Anonymous people take on a criminal charge and need counselling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks counselling as one example of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Counselling is a form of talking treatment, so an example of therapy.

clue.text: Smoke rising after choice, there's pope at last!

indicators.note: the final letter comes after the choice word

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: White smoke goes up after the cardinals' choice: a new pope at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is a papal conclave, where white smoke announces a new pope; here it is just a column of smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A plume is a column of smoke or vapour rising into the air.

clue.text: Quote to cover redevelopment of spacy urban scene

indicators.note: the quoting word wraps around the rest, which sits inside it

parts.note: to cite is to quote

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quote is sought for covering the redevelopment of a spacious site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quote' is a verb here, not a builder's estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cityscape is a view or picture of a town's buildings, so an urban scene.

clue.text: Possibly Bohemian-sounding threat to king

indicators.note: -sounding means a word that sounds like the Bohemian one, so we want its pronunciation, not its spelling

parts.note: a Bohemian may be a Czech, as Bohemia is part of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A bohemian type threatens a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that Bohemian is only one example of a Czech; 'Bohemian' tempts toward the arty sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, check is an attack on the opponent's king.

clue.text: Prime time not needed by such as Spielberg

indicators.note: the time letter is dropped from the director's name

parts.note: Steven Spielberg is the film director

explanation.surface: Prime time slots are not needed by a director like Spielberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime time' looks like a phrase about TV schedules, but Prime is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a prime number, divisible only by itself and one.

clue.text: Inventory is the thing hiding the beginning of the end

parts.note: it can stand for the thing, as in 'that's it'

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the end is concealed, so it is dropped

parts.note: demise means death, the end

explanation.surface: Taking stock is the key thing, hiding the start of the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' is a word for death; 'hiding the beginning of' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, which is what making an inventory means.

clue.text: Overlooking one at one, relief when withdrawing story

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so what is left is read backwards
to overlook something is to leave it out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: alleviation is relief from pain or distress
I is the Roman numeral for one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ignoring one-on-one sessions, someone is relieved to withdraw a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' removes I, AT, I from ALLEVIATION to leave ALLEVON; 'withdrawing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, so a type of story.

clue.text: Good socialist playwright appearing in acceptable flier

indicators.note: the playwright shows up inside the acceptable word

parts.note: OK means acceptable
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright and a Fabian socialist

explanation.surface: A worthy left-wing dramatist appears in a decent aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A goshawk is a bird of prey, and a bird is a flier.

clue.text: Uncontrolled area in middle of tarmac

indicators.note: the letter goes in the centre of the other word

parts.note: the tarmac is the airfield runway

explanation.surface: An unchecked area appears in the middle of the airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway vehicle or process is out of control.
